questions.answer: As the source approaches, successive wavefronts are closer together. More wavefronts reach the observer each second, so the observed frequency is higher even though the source frequency is unchanged.
accepted_alternatives: Wavefront compression in front of the approaching source increases the wavefront arrival rate at the observer.

marking_points.text: States that successive wavefronts are closer together in front of the approaching source.
Links the increased wavefront arrival rate to the higher observed frequency while source frequency remains unchanged.
